dives.name: 7th Street (Johannesburg)
dives.story: Welcome to 7th Street in Melville, a lively hub nestled in Johannesburg's Gauteng province. This vibrant street comes alive with a wonderful array of restaurants and bars, creating a buzzing atmosphere perfect for a relaxed evening out. It's a favourite spot, especially with students from the University of Johannesburg, bringing a youthful energy to its charming sidewalks. You might even recognise it from the popular South African soap opera 7de Laan, adding to its local charm and significance.
dives.best: The best way to experience 7th Street is to immerse yourself in its evening dining and social scene.
dives.tip: For a truly local feel, visit when the university students are out and about.

dives.name: Anglo-Boer War Memorial (Johannesburg)
dives.story: Welcome to a truly significant cultural landmark in Johannesburg, the Anglo-Boer War Memorial. This impressive site, originally known as the Rand Regiments Memorial, stands as a tribute to those who lost their lives during the Second Boer War. It was thoughtfully rededicated on 10 October 1999 to honor all people who died during that conflict, reflecting a more inclusive spirit of remembrance. Located right next door to the South African National Museum of Military History, it offers a profound opportunity for reflection. Visiting here allows you to connect with a crucial chapter of our nation's past.
dives.best: The best way to experience this memorial is to visit it alongside the South African National Museum of Military History.
dives.tip: You will find the memorial conveniently located right next door to the South African National Museum of Military History.

dives.name: Arbor Park
dives.story: Welcome to Arbor Park, a lively multi-use stadium right here in Newcastle, KwaZulu-Natal. This is where the heart of local football beats, a place filled with the energy of the game. Imagine the vibrant atmosphere as fans gather to support their teams, especially our very own Newcastle Sicilians F.C. It's a wonderful spot to connect with the community and experience the passion for sport that runs deep in South Africa. You'll feel the excitement and camaraderie that makes local matches so special.
dives.best: The best way to experience Arbor Park is to attend a football match.
dives.tip: Plan your visit around a Newcastle Sicilians F.C. home game in the Vodacom League for a true local experience.

dives.name: Arderne Gardens
dives.story: Welcome to Arderne Gardens, a true gem nestled in Claremont, Cape Town. This beautiful public park and arboretum, established way back in 1845, offers a serene escape. It's a place where you can feel the history and natural beauty intertwine, offering a peaceful retreat from the city bustle. Recognised as a South African Provincial Heritage Site, its charm is undeniable. You'll often see it bustling with joy, as it's a beloved spot for capturing beautiful wedding memories.
dives.best: It is a wonderful place to visit for a tranquil escape and to appreciate its natural beauty.
dives.tip: Keep an eye out for the many beautiful backdrops that make it a favourite for wedding photographers.

dives.name: Babylonstoren
dives.story: Welcome to Babylonstoren, nestled in the beautiful Drakenstein Valley of the Cape Winelands. This historic wine estate is home to one of South Africa's oldest Cape Dutch houses, offering a glimpse into our rich heritage. Its magnificent garden, designed by Patrice Taravella, is a true highlight, drawing inspiration from Cape Town's iconic Company's Garden. It's a place where history, nature, and design beautifully intertwine, often described as 'the Versailles of vegetable gardens' for its stunning beauty and meticulous layout. You'll feel a sense of peace and wonder wandering through its vibrant paths.
dives.best: The best way to experience Babylonstoren is to explore its magnificent garden.
dives.tip: Focus your visit on the magnificent garden, a true highlight of the estate.

dives.name: Baxter Theatre Centre
dives.story: Let me show you The Baxter Theatre Centre, a vibrant performing arts complex nestled in Cape Town's Rondebosch. Affectionately known as The Baxter, this cultural gem is a significant part of the University of Cape Town. It serves as a beloved stage where the Western Cape's finest theatre performers and artists bring their stories to life. Visiting The Baxter offers a wonderful opportunity to immerse yourself in the rich tapestry of South African creativity and experience the pulse of our local arts scene.
dives.best: The best way to experience The Baxter is by attending one of its captivating live performances.
dives.tip: When speaking with locals, you'll often hear it referred to simply as 'The Baxter'.

dives.name: Birds of Eden
dives.story: Welcome to Birds of Eden, a truly remarkable free-flight aviary and bird sanctuary in our beautiful Western Cape. Picture a vast mesh dome, thoughtfully built over 2.3 hectares of indigenous forest, creating an incredible natural habitat. Here, you can wander along 1.2 kilometres of pathways, with many elevated sections, allowing you to observe the diverse birdlife from every perspective. It's a place where you feel completely immersed in nature, surrounded by the vibrant sounds and sights of the sanctuary, making it a memorable stop near Plettenberg Bay.
dives.best: The best way to experience this sanctuary is by exploring the extensive walkways that wind through the forest.
dives.tip: Make sure to utilize the elevated sections of the walkways for unique views of the birds at all levels of the forest.

dives.name: Café Caprice
dives.story: Set directly on Camps Bay Beach in Cape Town, Café Caprice is a beach bar and restaurant overlooking the Atlantic Ocean. Founded by South African rugby player and restaurateur James Small, this venue holds a proud place in the city's coastal dining scene. Guests come to enjoy the oceanfront atmosphere alongside the café's noted cocktails. It also carries a distinct star appeal, having earned a reputation for the celebrities that frequent it. It is a wonderful stop to experience the seaside charm and social energy of the Western Cape.
dives.best: The best way to experience Café Caprice is by relaxing with one of their famous cocktails while taking in the views of the Atlantic Ocean.
dives.tip: Keep an eye out during your visit, as the café is widely known for attracting celebrity guests.
